chapter: Working with Al Grey and Diva
title: The New School: meeting Norman Simmons, Junior Mance and Al Grey
summary: At the New School she met Norman Simmons, who introduced her to Al and Clark Terry; Junior Mance was a karate black belt; a session led to Grey hiring her.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: No. I was so lucky when I first moved to New York. I went to the New School and the faculty was like a Who’s Who of living jazz giants, and it was amazing. And that’s where I met Norman [Simmons] and Norman introduced me to Al and to Clark Terry, and that’s where I met Junior, and then it turned out that Junior was a second degree black belt at the place I had just started taking karate.

And those were the days when it was hard to get to black belt. I mean not that it’s not hard now, but it was very physical, very hard core, more hard core than it is now on a fighting level. Yeah. So that was great, and he was such a nice guy, and obviously a great musician. I was so lucky, I met so many great people there and got to play with them. And then Norman introduced me to Al, he put me on a recording session of I don’t know if it was Al or somebody else, and they just brought me in to just play the saxophone parts and then they were just going to bring in whoever to overdub the solos and stuff, and then they decided that I did such a good job quote unquote that they left me on the recording, and that was when Al started hiring me. So things were really popping at that point, I really was so lucky. And Joe Williams — what a nice guy.
